newsitem.title: SPAIN: Japan copper smelting industry seen under pressure.
newsitem.headline: Japan copper smelting industry seen under pressure.

text.p: Japan's copper smelting industry is coming under increasing pressure, and the country will probably move more towards involvement in smelting operations in other countries, John Champagne, Chief operating officer at Global Minerals and Metals said.

"Japan's custom smelting industry has been squeezed by the the long-term strength of the yen, high operating costs, and the fall in the Japanese price of sulphuric acid, which reduces net-backs," Champagne said at Metal Bulletin's 10th International Copper Conference.

Another important factor is the gradual reduction of tariff barriers following the Uruguay Round of the GATT trade talks. The tariff used to be six percent, based on 15,000 yen/tonne, but is progressing lower to three percent of the value of the copper price by 1999, he said.
"This is a different environment that the Japanese smelting industry will have to live with," Champagne said.
There is thus little scope for smelter expansion in Japan. All that is likely to take place is upgrading, but no real new capacity will be added.
"In future, Japan is likely to be exporting its smelting technology," he said.
